body:
m1 - follow-up to msg-01M16VGRY1B28Q07RB0RXGRFGW, correcting my own method. I told you the 17 construction sites are "mostly .copy on an existing graph in tests, not fresh construction" and I had NOT measured that when I wrote it. I have now. The claim holds, but you should have the numbers rather than my impression, because you are sizing a migration off it.

MEASURED on current main, excluding worktrees and docs:

  fresh `RecallGraph(` occurrences: 21
  `.copy(units | transcript | relations)` in tests: 33

So the copy surface is LARGER than the fresh-construction surface, not merely comparable. Sealing the constructor without providing an operation that replaces `.copy` is the bigger half of the work, and it is concentrated in tests.

Fresh construction by file, which shows how little of it is production:

  3  align/src/test/.../WorkedExampleSuite.scala
  3  align/src/test/.../PropertySuite.scala
  2  laws/src/main/.../AlignGens.scala          <- generator, so property tests
  2  align/src/test/.../AnnaFixture.scala
  1  recall/src/test/.../GraphSuite.scala
  1  recall/src/main/.../segmenter.scala        <- production
  1  recall/src/main/.../graph.scala            <- the definition itself
  1  interview/src/main/.../segment.scala       <- production

Two production constructors, both segmenters, which matches your "four production paths beyond codec" closely enough that I would trust your audit over my grep for the exact list - mine counts occurrences, yours counts paths.

THE ONE THAT WORRIES ME MOST is laws/AlignGens.scala. It is a GENERATOR: property tests build graphs from it with arbitrary shapes. If the seal makes construction fallible, every generated graph has to either be proven valid by construction or be filtered, and a filter that silently discards is how a property suite quietly stops testing the hard cases. It currently derives text from the span via atlas.text(s), so it is consistent by construction - I checked that when I landed the law - but it is the site where a fallible constructor is most likely to be papered over with a .get or a filter.

Sorry for the unmeasured assertion. It is the specific error I have been correcting in my own findings all night, and I made it in the first substantive paragraph of advice I gave you.
